concept.name: Acceptance
concept.definition: In auction market theory, acceptance is the market demonstrating agreement with a price zone by spending time and doing volume there: repeated TPO prints and two-sided trade at a level show that both buyers and sellers are willing to transact at those prices. Acceptance inside a prior value area confirms balance; acceptance beyond it establishes value at new prices.
concept.intuition: Acceptance is the market lingering: if price arrives at a level and trade keeps happening there, the level is being treated as fair.
concept.mechanics: Judged from profile structure — time at price (multiple TPO periods), volume build-up, and overlapping distributions — rather than from a touch; e.g., several consecutive 30-minute periods printing beyond a breakout level constitute acceptance of the new area, while a quick probe and retreat does not.
concept.failure_modes: Acceptance is recognizable only as time passes, so acting on it is inherently late; and a zone accepted for days can be abandoned in minutes when new information arrives.
concept.misconceptions: Acceptance is not bullish or bearish by itself — it only says current prices are agreed as fair; acceptance above a breakout can still precede a full reversal back through the range.
concept.example: After gapping above the prior value area, price builds four consecutive TPO periods between 4,540 and 4,548 with heavy volume; the market has accepted the higher prices rather than rejecting the gap.

citations.source: GoCharting — Market Profile Trading: The Complete Guide (time spent at a price is acceptance)
FuturesIndicators — Trading With Market Profile: Practical Setups (acceptance above VAH vs rejection)
